reviews.review:
I'm placing this game at least right now as "Do not recommend" specifically in the context of english/non native speakers as at least right now the current bugs that I'm seeing for this game are egrigous enough that I believe that they will actually detract away from the experience along with a couple of things that particularly bother me with the way the developers handle their games in general, but don't necessarily give me a hard "Don't recommend" but more so "I don't recommend if you're expecting everything to be perfect"

Pros about this game so far from where I'm at
- The writing is superb, but this is expected given the writer of this is Kotaku
- The strengths of the writing carry out a lot of my gripes with this game and in general with games from Kotaku
- The visuals are superb
- The music is great

Without spoiling too hard, I think the details towards the writing for this game have a clear goal in mind that really make you think overall from my experience from the game where I currently am at the moment

- This actually works on handhelds mostly. This may not seem like a big deal but you'd be really surprised how many visual novels have elements to the games that make it non user friendly for people that don't want to strap themselves to a chair while playing these games. 

The cons that I believe can be fixed
- Text bubbles go off screen removing away dialogue
- Gramatical mistakes that normally I wouldn't be super picky about, but because this game is being carried so hard by the writing I think this needs to be fleshed out/fixed. 
- Translation errors that give confusion for important text shown in the game
- Some parts of the dialogue I believe that should be translated seemingly have not been at the moment to really hammer in the stakes for certain routes. 

Because the writing in this game is strongly carrying this game, when the mistakes arise it really takes away from the experience from the game, so if any bugs should be addressed, these should be in my opinion prioritized.

- Please please please, add a "skip to choice" option. I had the pleasure of running down the final scenario for the detective route a few times because I didn't realize who the real culprit was/ I could even select them as an option. To be clear, I think that element should be kept as those are the kind of things I love about these games, but jesus christ I don't need to retell the exact same sequence of events that I just got through that also has extremely long dialogue to skip through.

Cons that I don't believe can be fixed/ Grips

The below are core to the game and are more critiques for how this studio develops it's games. For context I have not played the Danganronpa series (will get to it eventually), but I've gone through some of the more recent stuff such as Hundred Line, Rain Code, and now this and in all of these games a theme I've noticed has been really bothering me.

- I don't mind having different "genres" being captured within the game if the studio wants to make the gameplay fresh, but the games need to be good/enjoyable. In this game I just got through playing the equivalent of a recapatcha for arranging photos to match the image that had a timer attached to it. I don't know who in the studio thought this was a great addition, but please, no.  I don't like doing those to verify my identity, and I sure as hell don't want it to be a mandatory requirement for me to clear the game that also has a timer attached to being able to solve it.

- The weaker areas that this studio is not known for making video game wise getting carried through the writing has been a theme I've noticed over the past few games. I've only done 2 of the routes so far, but the contrast between the detective route (this studios bread and butter), then going towards an escape style scenario is night and day. I also feel with the escape scenario the writing had more bugs on top of being a lot weaker than the previous scenario, which really makes going through dreaded phases terrible

And this isn't something that's unqiue to this game, I don't think that good writing should excuse poorly executed games. If this stuido wants to do different genres that cool, but they need to be at least solid enough to not feel like a mandatory chore to get through

- The music for this game while superb does rinse and repeat the same tonality between the 3 different games. If these were related in some way, easter eggs, or sequels than that would be fine, but in this case this seems to be done to basically create the same "mood" without really thinking to deeply to make something unique for this game. I like the music, so I'm fine with it, but stuff like this in my opinion should be considered as well when making your games. 

At least right now as of 11/17/2025, I would hold off a bit on buying this game for a couple of months then check back to see if updates are made. Since the launch of the game when I purchase there have been some bug patches that have been posted so I do think they're aware of some of the issues. This was similar to hundred line's initial release where nearly all of the dialogue was slow/unskippable then subsequent updates gave better player experience.
